ui.name: Charlotte
ui.title_cos: Costner Law, Fairway Title, Anchor Title, all in Charlotte
ui.law: North Carolina is an attorney-closing state: a licensed NC attorney must handle the closing, so your title company is a law firm. You can assign a purchase contract; tell the seller in writing that you may assign it and never market the house itself.
ui.groups: "Metrolina REIA", "Charlotte Real Estate Investors", "NC Wholesale Deals"
ui.prefc: Code cases: the city posts every open housing and nuisance case and every order to demolish. A housing case means an inspector found the house unsafe or unfit; the owner is paying fines or facing repairs they often cannot afford.
ui.buyers_note: Companies that bought 2 or more houses in the last 18 months, from the county sale data, most active first. Skip the big institutions and builders; the 2 to 20 purchase LLCs are the ones who buy wholesale deals. Look up the owner on the NC Secretary of State and call.
ui.buyers_empty: No buyers found in the sale data yet.
ui.repairs: Repairs, Charlotte rough numbers per house: cosmetic 15-25k, kitchen+baths 30-50k, roof 12-20k, HVAC 8-14k, crawlspace and moisture 5-15k, full gut 60-100k.
ui.sources: Mecklenburg County assessor ownership layer (owner, mailing address, value, sale), City of Charlotte code enforcement open cases and orders to demolish
